finding: Notion SubagentLifecycle cancels unfinished siblings after one run_many child fails, then removes their task ids. The current regression explicitly calls a cancelled child safe to retry, but cancellation does not prove that local/provider side effects did not already happen. A sibling that mutated state before cancellation can therefore be retried with the same logical task id and repeat the side effect. The lifecycle has no durable completed/uncertain child ledger.
cross_project_contract: Qwen coding subagents already persist running/uncertain/done state and block automatic retry after possible mutating tool side effects. A future Qwen delegation adapter must preserve this invariant instead of flattening QWEN_SUBAGENT_AGENT_UNCERTAIN_RETRY_BLOCKED into a generic retryable delegation failure.
recommended_owner_action: Replace the existing 'cancelled child ... safe retry' assumption with a fail-closed uncertainty regression.
Do not enable side-effect-capable run_many as automatically retryable all-or-nothing work until per-child durable outcome/uncertainty survives cancellation and restart.
For the Qwen adapter, map delegation task identity to a stable persisted Qwen batch/task identity and preserve uncertain status.
For Notion local-tool children, add an equivalent accepted-tool/side-effect checkpoint before automatic retry is allowed.
Do not lose already completed sibling outcomes when a different child fails.
